newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan vice-president to visit Europe - newspaper.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan vice-president to visit Europe - newspaper.

text.p: Taiwan Vice-President Lien Chan will visit Europe on the way home from an official trip to Nicaragua, the United Evening News said on Tuesday.
The newspaper, quoting unnamed high-level officials, said Lien would fly to "important" and "powerful" European nations to work on isolated Taipei's diplomatic relationships.
Lien, who is also premier, is scheduled to leave for Nicaragua on Tuesday to attend the January 10 inauguration of President-elect Arnoldo Aleman.
He will stop in New York on his way home.

Communist China, Taiwan's arch rival since a civil war split them in 1949, regards the island as a rebel province ineligible for foreign ties. It has tightened a diplomatic squeeze on Taipei in its quest to bring Taiwan under mainland rule.
Only 30 countries, mostly poor states in Africa and central America, recognise Taiwan's exiled Republic of China government instead of Beijing's communist Chinese government.
South Africa, Taiwan's biggest ally, announced in November it would sever ties with Taipei by the end of 1997 in favour of Beijing.
To evade China's diplomatic embargo, Taiwan officials have been engaging in "secret diplomacy" -- unannounced visits to countries which recognise Beijing instead of Taipei.
Foreign Minister John Chang and Lien have between them visited Ukraine, Singapore, Malaysia, Belgium, the United Arab Emirates and Jordan over the last year.
